name: FLIPoQ GmbH
description: FLIPoQ’s unique 3D printing mesh-technology (FLIPoQ- Functional Large Isotropic parts in original material Quality) allows to create 3D-geometries from any space certified polymer material in a reliable way. For space applications it is essential to meet dimensional precision and accuracy and to follow strict quality control processes to guarantee the functionality of 3d printed parts under roughest conditions. But first of all – you need to be able to work any certified polymer material – this is the unique selling position of FLIPoQ. With the SPACEoQ-proposal (supportless Polymers with Aerospace Certification for Earth or Mars in original material Quality) we want to discover new opportunities of our processes in space. We make it possible for the clients to produce spare and series parts in any required polymer material. Misprints can be recycled and worthful and expensive materials can be saved in a sustainable production way. Our technology works sustainable saving support structures and making it possible to 3D print high-performance materials with low energy input and possibly decreased cycle times (no heated-up build chamber). Our process creates parts, that demand less post-processing compared to traditional processes.

name: GEDYTE GmbH i.G. (in formation)
description: GEDYTE, founded by entrepreneur Tizian Kernstock, is building an intelligent assistant for small and mid-scale greenhouses. The company targets controlled-environment agriculture, helping private and light-commercial growers plan, monitor and optimise crops with a low-cost sensor box and a mobile app that turns data into clear, actionable guidance and yield forecasts. GEDYTE fuses on-site measurements with satellite Earth-observation data and weather to generate micro-climate insights and short-term yield and readiness predictions. Using EO provides broad, consistent coverage beyond the sensors, improves model robustness, and enables possible features such as benchmarking against local radiation patterns, early stress detection signals, and more reliable recommendations when in-situ data are sparse. By bringing space-enabled intelligence to affordable greenhouse tools, GEDYTE aims to raise yield, reduce resource use, and make predictable, high-quality harvests accessible to non-industrial growers.

name: Geocledian
description: Founded in 2013, Geocledian is designing and providing custom crop monitoring solutions based on satellite technology. For this purpose, Geocledian has developed the comprehensive Ag|Knowledge V4 API, a crop monitoring platform providing near real-time analysis ready data, analytics tools and crop modelling with more than 70 different endpoints. It enables users to integrate remote sensing and weather-based crop analytics into end-user applications or workflow management systems with minimum effort and development time. These custom solutions can be tuned to a large variety of crops, cultivation types and regions. They may range from determining optimum harvesting dates for grains, to validating the provenance of a variety of supplied goods to fulfil contract obligations, or is enabling sugar mills to efficiently deal with thousands of small growers fields. Geocledian has built and improved this platform over the last 9 years. It uses open satellite data from Sentinel, Landsat but is also integrating commercial weather data and other datasets. Our Ag|Knowledge product is successfully used by multiple farm management systems, mobile apps and with governments with a customer focus on Europe and Asia.

Machine learning integrates naturally as a crucial component for geo applications. During incubationthey will develop their existing prototype for machine learning using Random Forests into a working product. They plan to design use cases and implement billing and cost estimation. Founders are a database research group of the University of Marburg, who started with Geo Engine GmbH in 2021 and our first applicant from from Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen Gießen.
